tagline: Power RSS reader with rules, monitoring, search, and automations.
verdictSummary: A single-user RSS reader with keyword rules and alerts is a real weekend build on top of well-understood feed-parsing libraries, though it won't match Inoreader's scale or years of polish. What it does cover is the actual daily loop: fetch feeds, apply rules, get alerted, search everything you've read.
coreLoopDIY: Fetch feeds on a schedule, apply keyword rules per feed or folder, tag and file articles automatically, and alert on matches.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for reliability and a power-user rules engine that keeps working even as individual feeds break or change — not because RSS parsing itself is hard.
notes: A useful power-user yes — RSS remains an open protocol, and that openness is exactly what makes this buildable.
prompt:
Build a single-user RSS reader with rules and alerts: fetch a list of feeds on a schedule, parse new items, and dedupe them by their feed-provided ID. Import an existing OPML export on first run so nothing has to be retyped, and support exporting the current subscription list back out. Build a three-pane reading UI — folders, article list, reading pane — with keyboard navigation and per-folder unread counts. Add keyword rules scoped to a feed or a folder, matching on title or body text, with actions to tag, mark read, or send an alert by email or push notification. Build full-text search across every stored article. Mark a feed as failing after several consecutive fetch errors so broken feeds don't silently go stale.

Do not build mobile apps, article translation, or third-party integrations — adding a new feed means editing the OPML or the UI directly, which is a fine trade for owning your reading list and rules.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Inoreader subscriptions?
faq.a: Yes — Inoreader exports a standard OPML file with your feeds and folders, and importing that on first run is exactly how this build expects to be set up.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: As a responsive web page, yes, if hosted somewhere reachable. There's no dedicated mobile app or offline sync.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting and a database, typically a few dollars a month — genuinely inexpensive since RSS traffic and storage are both small.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Scale and polish under load. Inoreader handles thousands of feeds reliably with years of edge-case handling; a personal build works well at a personal feed count but hasn't been stress-tested the way a mature product has.
